> Dozable 0.52.52 — canary; not the Homebrew stable release. The stable manual is https://dozable.com/docs/ (https://dozable.com/llms.txt).

# Dozable 0.52.52 — the manual

> Fast, resumable, secure Linux sandboxes for AI coding agents on your Mac — your API keys never go inside.

The user manual of doz 0.52.52, carried inside it: every page as Markdown, in this folder. `doz docs PAGE` prints one (a name or a number), `doz docs --path` prints this folder. The same manual online, for this version only: https://dozable.com/v/0.52.52/llms.txt

## Docs

- [Getting started](01-getting-started.md): Dozable runs AI coding agents, such as Claude Code, in small Linux virtual machines on your Mac.
- [Installing, upgrading and uninstalling](02-install-upgrade-uninstall.md): doz is one command-line program.
- [Setting up this Mac](03-setting-up.md): Setup — onboarding — is what you do once after installing: it checks your Mac, prepares the base image every tool is added to, adds the keys your tools use, chooses and confirms what sandboxes may use as you (Access: GitHub, your SSH agent), explains folder rules and lets you choose what they do, writes your settings, and makes your first sandbox.
- [Projects](04-projects.md): A project is a folder with a doz_project.yaml file in it.
- [Sandboxes and their lifecycle](05-sandboxes-and-lifecycle.md): A sandbox is one Linux virtual machine with its own disks.
- [The dashboard (doz ui)](06-the-dashboard.md): doz ui is Dozable in your browser: every sandbox with a live terminal, its restore points and permissions, your images, accounts, disk use and settings.
- [Terminals and sessions](07-terminals-and-sessions.md): A session is a terminal program running inside a sandbox: a shell, claude, pi, a dev server.
- [Images and bases](08-images-and-bases.md): Every sandbox starts from a baked image: a disk with a Linux system, a developer toolkit and, usually, the agent a recipe installs.
- [Agents and accounts](09-agents-and-accounts.md): Dozable runs three AI coding agents out of the box — Claude Code, pi and OpenAI's Codex — and gives each one the account it should use, without the secret ever entering the sandbox.
- [What the agent can do: permissions and the network](10-permissions-and-network.md): A sandbox has no network card.
- [Signing in from a sandbox](11-signing-in-from-a-sandbox.md): Many command-line tools sign you in through a web browser: they open a sign-in page, you sign in, and the provider sends your browser back to the tool on http://localhost:PORT.
- [Restore points, duplicates and saved disks](12-restore-points-duplicates-templates.md): Three ways to copy a sandbox's disk, each instant (they're APFS clones, sharing space until something changes):
- [Resources and disk space](13-resources-and-disk-space.md): Dozable keeps everything in one folder, the store.
- [Letting another agent drive Dozable](14-letting-another-agent-drive.md): So far you have run doz.
- [Settings reference](15-settings-reference.md): This Mac's settings are in one file, ~/.config/doz/doz.toml (under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME when that is set).
- [Security model](16-security-model.md): Dozable's job is to let an AI agent work freely — install things, run code, make a mess — without putting your Mac, your credentials or your data at risk.
- [Troubleshooting and FAQ](17-troubleshooting-and-faq.md): doz doctor checks everything Dozable depends on — macOS and Apple silicon, the virtualization permission, the Linux kernel, the NAT helper, disk space, the daemon, your Claude login and your images — and says what to do about anything that fails.
- [GitHub as you](18-github.md): An agent on your Mac uses git and gh as you: it clones your private repositories, opens pull requests, comments on issues.
- [Managed tools](19-the-tools-layer.md): Some settings need a tool inside the sandbox to be useful: "GitHub as you" is best with gh, SSH agent forwarding needs an ssh client and GitHub's host keys, tmux sessions need tmux.
- [Folder rules: .dozignore and .dozreadonly](20-workspace-rules.md): A sandbox's /workspace is your Mac folder, live.
- [The folder view (dozview)](21-the-workspace-view.md): /workspace inside a sandbox is not your shared folder itself: it is a live view of it, served by a small Dozable program, dozview.
- [Prompts for your agent](22-prompts-for-your-agent.md): Your Mac's own coding agent — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor — can install Dozable, set it up and run sandboxes for you.
- [Sound](23-sound.md): A sandbox can have sound: programs in it play through your Mac's speakers and, if you want, record from its microphone.
- [Codex](24-codex.md): OpenAI's Codex runs in a Dozable sandbox the way Claude Code does: ready to work, without approval prompts (the VM and its network are the boundary), told where it runs, and with its credential kept on your Mac — it never enters the sandbox.
- [The dashboard on your other computers, tablets and phones (doz ui --lan)](25-doz-serve.md): doz ui is one dashboard.
- [Trying agents, and what Dozable supports](26-try-and-search.md): doz try takes you from nothing to talking to an agent in one command.
- [More agents: Antigravity CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot CLI, Qwen Code, Goose, Kilo Code CLI, Mistral Vibe, Factory Droid, Dirac, Kimi Code, Cline CLI, OpenHands CLI, Letta Code, Docker Agent, Nanocoder, mini-swe-agent, Open Interpreter, Crush, MiMo Code, CodeWhale, Maki, oh-my-pi, Tau, Gemini CLI](27-more-agents.md): Beside Claude Code, pi and Codex, Dozable runs agents from other makers.
- [Other AI tools](28-ai-tools.md): Beside the coding agents, Dozable runs AI tools that are not coding agents: command-line tools that answer a prompt, prompt toolkits, agent frameworks.
- [Web ports: opening a sandbox's web page on your Mac](29-web-ports.md): Some tools serve a web page from inside the sandbox: a chat playground, a workflow editor, the dev server of the app you are building.
- [Your own recipes, and community catalogues](30-your-own-recipes.md): Every tool Dozable runs comes from a recipe: a YAML file that says how the tool is installed, how it runs, which key it uses and what it may reach.
- [Your dotfiles](31-dotfiles.md): A new sandbox has a stock shell: no aliases, no prompt of yours, no editor settings.
- [Claude Code with other models — a gateway, or a model server on your Mac](32-claude-code-other-models.md): Claude Code talks to Anthropic by default: this Mac's Claude login, a setup token or an Anthropic API key, exactly as in Agents and accounts.
- [Bundling doz in an app](33-bundling-doz-in-an-app.md): Most people do not need this page.
- [Sessions on this Mac](34-sessions-on-this-mac.md): Every other page of this manual is about sandboxes: a program in its own small Linux machine, with a network that reaches only what you allow and none of your keys.
- [The menu bar app](35-the-menu-bar-app.md): Dozable's daemon is the background process that runs your sandboxes.
- [Chat](36-chat.md): Chat is a set of rooms on your Mac where you and your agents talk: you in the dashboard or a terminal, each agent with its own token.
- [Workspaces](37-workspaces.md): A workspace is an environment set up for getting work done: its agents, its rooms, the brief that says what the work is for, and any folders it works on (usually projects).
- [Agents / Bots](38-agents-and-bots.md): An Agent / Bot is a lasting identity in chat: a participant with a name that stays, its agent program (Claude Code, Codex, …), its model and account, where it runs, how the chat server reaches it, and a token of its own.
- [Space files](39-space-files.md): A space file describes a workspace in one YAML file, NAME.space.yaml, kept in git beside the work: its agents, its rooms, the brief, any folders and sandboxes.
- [History and retention](40-history-and-retention.md): Dozable keeps a history of what happened on this Mac — every action on a sandbox, sessions, the daemon's runs and its events, each sandbox's connections and network by minute, CPU, memory and disk samples, the use of your keys (by name), workspace and permission logs, runs and their frames, and the times of chat messages and the outcomes of Asks — and answers it as one timeline: doz timeline.
- [The manual — contents](README.md): every chapter, and when to read it.
